title: Uniform convergence and continuity from a summable uniform norm bound
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$, so $|x|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $|1|=1$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, and $|x+y|\le |x|+|y|$. Assume the metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|$ is complete. Let $X$ be a topological space, $S\subseteq X$, $f_n:X\to K$ for $n\ge0$, and $u_n\in\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ with $\sum_{n\ge0}u_n$ summable (the net of finite subsums converges). Suppose $|f_n(x)|\le u_n$ for every $n\ge0$ and $x\in S$. Then the partial sums $\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}f_n(x)$ converge uniformly on $S$ to $F(x)=\sum_{n\ge0}f_n(x)$. If every $f_n$ is continuous on $S$ with its subspace topology, then $F$ is continuous on $S$.
